[[Category:English terms with audio pronunciation|UGH]] ===Interjection=== ugh[[Category:English lemmas|UGH]][[Category:English interjections|UGH]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|UGH]][[Category:Pages with entries|UGH]][[Category:Pages with 4 entries|UGH]] # Used to express [[:repugnance#English|repugnance]], [[:disgust#English|disgust]], or [[:annoyance#English|annoyance]]. #: Synonyms: ''see'' [[Thesaurus:yuck#English|Thesaurus:yuck]] #:
'''Ugh'''! The bread in the pantry has gone moldy.
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|UGH]] #*
'''1855''', [[:w:Robert Browning|Robert Browning]], [[:s:Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came|Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came]], section XXI:[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
[...] It may have been a water-rat I speared, / But, '''ugh'''! it sounded like a baby's shriek.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
#*
'''1886''', [[:w:Peter Christen Asbjørnsen|Peter Christen Asbjørnsen]], translated by H.L. Brækstad, Folk and Fairy Tales, page 57:[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
"'''Ugh,''' what a smell of Christian blood there is here," screamed the giant.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
#*
'''2023''', “Paint The Town Red”, in Scarlet, performed by [[:w:Doja Cat|Doja Cat]]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
'''Ugh''', you can't take that bitch nowhere
[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
# Used to express inarticulate vocalisations, such as used by a caveman. #*
'''1921''', [[:w:H. G. Wells|H.G. Wells]], “The Grisly Folk”, in Selected Short Stories, published 1958, page 291:[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
The brothers surveyed the wide prospect earnestly. "'''Ugh'''!" said one abruptly and pointed. "'''Ugh'''!" cried his brother. The eyes of the whole tribe swung round to the pointing finger. The group became one rigid stare.
[[Category:English terms with quotations|UGH]]
